newsitem.title: CHINA: Ignorance barrier to China insurance market.
newsitem.headline: Ignorance barrier to China insurance market.

text.p: China has a huge potential market for life insurance but most Chinese don't know how to buy a policy or how insurance works, a Western industry official said on Thursday.

"China stands on the threshold of a new life insurance era, with rapidly growing numbers of people needing life insurance and being able to purchase it," said Geoff Tomlinson, group managing director of National Mutual Holdings Ltd.

A survey conducted by National Mutual in 50 major Chinese cities earlier this year estimated that just nine percent of those surveyed had any form of life insurance, Tomlinson told a business conference in Beijing.
The survey results had been projected to cover the top 70 percent of urban household incomes, representing 180 million people, he said.
"Many survey indicators pointed to a lack of knowledge regarding life insurance and suggest an enormous need for education in order to develop the market," he said.
About 74 percent of those surveyed said they were not familiar with life insurance, he said.
"Urban Chinese consumers tend not to be familiar with how it (life insurance) works, or aware of specific benefits they might receive," he said.

Many Chinese were keenly interested in caring for the elderly and providing for their children's education, yet had no plans for the financial well-being of their families in the event of premature death, he said.
"One urgent task is needed -- a public education campaign on the nature and benefits of life insurance," he said.
Industry analysts say China's insurance industry is still relatively undeveloped but is expanding fast.
Official figures show the sector took in 72.5 billion yuan in premiums in 1995, an increase of 10.4 percent from 1994. Premium income is forecast to balloon to 120 billion yuan by the year 2000.

Scores of foreign insurers have opened representative offices in China but only two firms -- American International Assurance Co Ltd and Japan's Tokio Marine and Fire Insurance Co Ltd -- are allowed to issue policies.
